pages.title: The harbor after the rain
blocks: At dawn the fishing boats returned to a harbor that looked different from the one they had left. A week of rain had moved sand across the entrance.
The harbor master measured the channel before allowing the larger boats through. Smaller crews waited beside the old warehouse.

The delay lasted less than an hour, but it exposed a problem that residents had discussed for years. Every storm changed the route into the port.
‘We used to read the tide from the steps,’ said the retired pilot. ‘Now the steps are beneath the water.’

pages.title: Why the queue stopped twice
blocks: The queue appeared healthy until two workers finished at the same time. Each worker believed it had received the last available task.

const task = await queue.claim();
if (task) await processTask(task);
Claiming a task must be atomic. Otherwise a second worker can observe state that the first worker has already changed.
Five queue systems to try in your next project
A later failure came from cancellation. The response from an old request arrived after a new job had taken ownership of the interface.

pages.title: The room above the library
blocks: I first saw the room when the librarian asked me to carry a box upstairs. Its windows faced a courtyard I had never noticed from the street.
There were no shelves yet. A table stood in the middle, with one chair beside each of its four corners.

We opened the boxes slowly. The books had come from a school that was closing, and many still carried the names of former pupils.
‘A library is a promise that someone else may need what you have finished with,’ she told me.

The newspaper subscription lay on the table. It belonged to the library, which paid so that visitors could read without having to buy their own copies.
By three o’clock the room had filled with people who had no reason to know one another. The courtyard made the building feel larger.
